ai.description: This small frog reaches 30–40 mm. It is brown with a dark lateral band and a pale snout tip. Key features include long, slender limbs and prominent, pointed toe tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana bhadrai* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-colored lateral bands that extend from the snout through the eyes to the flanks, contrasting with a pale dorsum.
ai.habitat: The Bhadra Leaping Frog inhabits the leaf litter of evergreen forests and riparian zones within the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Bhadra leaping frog is primarily nocturnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among damp leaf litter and rocky stream banks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana bhadrai* is an egg-laying frog that breeds during the monsoon. Females deposit small clutches of eggs on moist, moss-covered rocks near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana bhadrai* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India, typically inhabiting moist evergreen forests at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Indirana bhadrai* produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard near rocky streams in evergreen forests during the monsoon.
